Q1 — Implementation language
facets.summary: The language is Rust, with a WebAssembly build of the same crate for editor and browser embedding.

facets.title: Q2 — Schema format
facets.summary: YAML 1.2 is the concrete syntax, and Headwater owns the schema language, the reference sublanguage, the overlay language and the meta-schema.

facets.title: Q3 — How much of the default taxonomy ships in the box
facets.summary: The base package is minimal and derived from the core, and optional content ships as add-only bundles.

facets.title: Q4 — Relation storage
facets.summary: Front matter is authoritative, and a relation instance is an object rather than a pointer.

facets.title: Q5 — Voice checking depth
facets.summary: Voice checking stays lexical, with a curated pattern set, a per-category posture and a reasoned escape hatch.

facets.title: Q6 — Where the corpus graph lives at rest
facets.summary: The graph never rests. Every run rebuilds it, and no derived artifact is canonical for anything.

facets.title: Q7 — Scope of the MCP surface
facets.summary: Three classes of tool, and a landed write never ships.

facets.title: Q8 — Probe cost and cadence
facets.summary: A probe is a document with a declared expectation, and cadence follows the purpose of the run.

facets.title: Q9 — Multi-repository corpora
facets.summary: A repository holds one or more corpora, the tier above harvests pinned exports, and no merged graph exists.

facets.title: Q10 — Naming
facets.summary: The name is Headwater, capitalized in prose and lower case as an identifier.

facets.title: Q11 — License and distribution posture
facets.summary: Apache-2.0 for the engine, the library, the base package and the bundles, ratified by the owner on 2026-08-11.

facets.title: Q12 — Migration path for an existing corpus
facets.summary: Adoption is a migration from no taxonomy, and `headwater infer` computes the adoption payload.

facets.title: Q13 — LinkML and SHACL as substrate
facets.summary: Headwater owns the language, emitters never chain, and LinkML is the last of six siblings.

facets.title: Q14 — Discovery surface
facets.summary: The corpus descriptor is a generated projection at `.headwater/corpus.json`, and registration went to Q16.

facets.title: Q15 — A synthesized content tier
facets.summary: Every document carries a warrant from a closed set of four, and `asserted` content is admitted with limits.

facets.title: Q16 — Public presence
facets.summary: Registration needs a channel with an obliged reader, a directory of corpora is refused, and the site is a projection of this corpus.

facets.title: Q17 — Governed access and the solution layer
facets.summary: The serving boundary is the export step of each publishing corpus. A profile filters for an audience, and Headwater has no principals.

facets.title: Q18 — Recording adjudicated disagreements
facets.summary: The edge does not become a node. An adjudication is a decision document that carries `overrides`.

facets.title: Q19 — Inbound integration: an external system of record
facets.summary: Imported content is `transcribed` against a committed pin, and an imported edge carries full weight from the first release.

facets.title: Q20 — Where scent lives
facets.summary: An optional source-owned cue sits on a relation instance, graded against the alternatives in view at the point of decision.

facets.title: Q21 — Terminological succession, and validity under merge
facets.summary: A retired-term lexicon sits in the language regime, and a verdict reports the read set that a merge may void.

A package digest checks a fetched artifact against a pin that a person committed, and it is never a signature. The in-house SHA-256 is held against a second implementation rather than replaced by a dependency.
facets.title: Q22 — The integrity posture of a published package

facets.summary: A published Rust guideline set is not installed as a skill, because a skill carries no rule of its own. Twenty-two lints are declared once in the workspace manifest, and each was chosen by measuring the corpus rather than by adopting a list.
facets.title: Q23 — The engine lint floor

facets.summary: Readability is not a sweep class and gets no verb, because every class of a sweep names two things that do not fit and a readability finding names one. A source file is not a slice member, because admitting one degrades the membership refusal for every class.
facets.title: Q24 — Readability, and what a sweep can be asked about

facets.summary: The namespace opens every identifier, and a published source declares no namespace at all, because any constant it wrote would be minted by every adopter of it at once.
facets.title: Q25 — Where the namespace goes in an identifier, and who declares it

facets.summary: Terminality stays a property of a state alone, because the per-regime reading is available at both call sites and costs the deferral that keeps one defect one finding. No published tradition wants the collision, and two that met it minted a second state name.
facets.title: Q26 — Whether terminality belongs to a state, or to a state and a regime

facets.summary: A decision record is governed prose, and the overlay binds the house language regime to it. The shelf carries a prose problem rather than a quotation problem, and collapsing all 37 inline quotations moves 64 findings to 63.
facets.title: Q27 — Whether a decision record is governed prose

facets.summary: An evaluation is governed prose, and the overlay binds the house language regime to it. The shelf carries 432 advisory findings, and the measurement that explains them is whether a rule was reading the prose when it was written rather than who wrote it.
facets.title: Q28 — Whether an evaluation is governed prose

facets.summary: The corpus root stays `docs`, because a path is corpus content only where a file with no front matter is a defect, and 185 of the 186 Markdown files under `engine/` exist to be defective. An interface contract lives inside the root and reaches a crate by a `governs` edge that binds on existence alone.
facets.title: Q29 — Whether a corpus root may contain code, and what an interface contract may reach

facets.summary: What an obligation waits on is a state and not a property, and the closed set holds four values. A required `waiting_on` facet on `obligation_record` takes `ruling`, `build`, `measurement` or `adopter`, and the decision-record bundle declares it.
facets.title: Q30 — Whether what an obligation waits on is a state or a property, and how many values it takes

facets.summary: This repository becomes public, and the date is unset. A settled posture with a pending date is not an open question, and the record is what stops each run from raising it as one.
facets.title: Q31 — Whether this repository becomes public, and when

facets.summary: The `self-audit` label states the reader test and not the provenance test. How a finding was found is not the test, and the only question is whether a reader outside this repository is better off.
facets.title: Q32 — Which test the self-audit label states

facets.summary: `clap` derives the command line for 17 lock entries, and a flag belongs to the verb that reads it rather than to the binary.
facets.title: Q33 — Whether the command line is derived, and who a flag belongs to

facets.summary: Acceptance is the merge onto main. A provenance block on an unmerged branch is a proposal, so an agent may write `accepted_by` there, and stop rule 5 binds main rather than the byte.
facets.title: Q34 — Whether acceptance means merged to main, and what an agent may write before that

facets.summary: The `requirement` and `acceptance_criterion` kinds serve the authored population alone. A transcribed requirement is a marked file that answers no contract, so a separate kind with an empty contract carries the imported case.
facets.title: Q35 — Whether one requirement kind holds an imported requirement and an authored one

facets.summary: Q17 counts a withheld anchor, and nothing says whether the count needs a class beside it.

facets.title: Whether an adjudication is ever partial
facets.summary: Q18 records an adjudication over a pair, and nothing says what happens when each document governs a different axis.

facets.title: The size of a committed snapshot with full requirement text
facets.summary: Q19 pins an external system of record, and nobody has measured what a snapshot with full requirement text costs.

facets.title: Whether the read set of a real corpus is small enough that publishing it is free
facets.summary: Publishing the read set costs 0.37 per cent of this corpus, and the fraction is a ratio against document size rather than a constant.

facets.title: Two documents state what voids a verdict, and they do not agree
facets.summary: Spec 12 voids a verdict by a tree diff, and the engine voids it by a hash comparison that no added document reaches.

facets.title: The front-matter half of a patch has no writer
facets.summary: Three documents name a mechanical correction inside front matter, and the two patch shapes that ship reach a run of prose and a relations block.

facets.title: A governs edge reaches the path it names and nothing under it
facets.summary: Impact detection compares the edited path against the anchor by equality, so an edge onto a directory answers for no file inside it.

facets.title: Nothing plays the hook role that two relations name as their author
facets.summary: `governs` and `traces_to` declare `created_by: hook`, no verb of this engine writes either one, and every such edge in this corpus is hand entry.

facets.title: A shelf layout names a file at birth and no rule reads it
facets.summary: A shelf layout is read by the scaffolder and by nothing else, and a rule that read it would report every document that a person renamed or typed by hand.

facets.title: The base package ships a kind that the scaffolder refuses to write
facets.summary: `kinds.specification` names no identifier scheme and four relations may name a document of it, so `headwater new specification` refuses on the stock package and no check reports the cause.

facets.title: An agent writes the acceptance stamp of every document in this corpus
facets.summary: Stop rule 5 forbids an agent to write `accepted_by`, and 161 of the 161 agent-drafted documents here carry one that the drafting agent typed.

facets.title: The capture-cost denominator is set by declaration and not by work
facets.summary: Over the eight scaffoldable kinds the verb supplies 48 of 56 units, the one hand entry of each kind is the summary, and the body counts nowhere.

facets.title: The loss census carries a finding by substring, so an index of rules and paths passes it
facets.summary: The audit that holds a format to its loss set asks whether the bytes contain a rule name and a path, and a text report with no findings block at all carried 39 of 45.

facets.title: The capture-cost surface names an entry point and never the caller
facets.summary: The store records which wire a run of the authoring verb arrived on, and an agent drove both wires on the day the term arrived.

facets.title: A surface cannot move the assisted fraction of a run
facets.summary: The four counts of a reading are derived from the plan, and a plan is the same plan whatever asked for it, so Q7's comparison has to read reach rather than the fraction.

facets.title: Every check passes a document that is still the scaffolder's placeholder
facets.summary: A decision record whose three sections each read TODO raised no finding at all, and the count over the corpus did not move.
The register holds no coherence obligation at all, and the one mechanism that could bind the sweep to one reports it verified from the declaration alone.
facets.title: A control that names a sweep marks its obligation verified with nothing run

facets.summary: A consumer that vendors a package for the first time takes the publisher's identity on the channel that carried the digest, because nothing signs a release and no key reaches an adopter.
facets.title: A pinned digest authenticates the pin and never the publisher

facets.summary: An import writes an edge onto an anchor kind, one resolver ships, and it reads the source tree, so the check layer reports every imported edge as unresolved.
facets.title: No anchor resolver reads a committed snapshot, so every imported edge lands unresolved

facets.summary: The read set of an edge instance holds the declaring document, so a target outside the corpus is in no key and a cached run reports what an uncached run does not.
facets.title: A cached verdict about an anchor survives the change that falsifies it

facets.summary: The read set artifact holds one line per document, so an external anchor is on no line and a gate that compares listed hashes cannot see the target of one leave the tree.
facets.title: The published read set names no anchor, so a gate decides nothing about one

facets.summary: Of the six readings `taxonomy audit` takes, one has a number a taxonomy states and five have none, so five report a population and no verdict.
facets.title: An audit reading carries no declared bar, so a distribution cannot become a finding

facets.summary: A waiver mechanism now ships and reads a conformance rule, so the coverage account of `headwater check` is the one reader of the pair that does not exist.
facets.title: No reader takes a waiver against a check finding, so one arm of the escape partition is empty

facets.summary: Three of the seven conformance rules can never be met, because the attestation each one names has no record format, and four rungs of the ladder wait behind them.
facets.title: Three conformance rules name an attestation that no record format exists for

facets.summary: A conformance rule set is held by the release digest and never by the lock, so a repository that takes its package from source can edit the rules its own gate reads.
facets.title: Nothing holds the conformance rule set of a package a consumer takes from source

facets.summary: Two rules of the language meet on a facet whose value is the author's judgment, and a sentinel is what the corpus wrote instead.
facets.title: A facet that applies to one value of another facet has nowhere to say so

facets.summary: The grader writes verdicts to standard output, no kind types a result, and the standing test spec 12 names cannot run.
facets.title: A probe result is printed and never committed, so nothing regenerates one

facets.summary: Spec 3 closes the warrant vocabulary at four values, nine documents here state a fifth, no check reads a warrant, and the query surface serves an unknown value as a vouched one.
facets.title: Nine documents state a warrant the closed set does not hold, and no check reads one

facets.summary: Spec 3 rules that an `asserted` document cannot carry `last_verified`. The facet contract requires it on every kind that has one, and nine of nine asserted documents carry it.
facets.title: Every asserted document carries the freshness date that spec 3 says it cannot

facets.summary: A path a change named that no census row holds keeps its prior version only where that version parsed, so a deleted document with malformed front matter reaches no rule.
facets.title: A deletion is invisible where the version that stood there does not parse

facets.summary: Q29 keeps the engine outside the corpus root, so a contract may name a crate and nothing names a crate that has no contract. A participation expectation runs between documents, and an anchor target is no node with a kind.
facets.title: Nothing holds a crate to having a contract under a root that excludes it

facets.summary: Spec 12 lists an unparseable file and an unclassifiable path among the structural findings of Phase A, and the engine emits no finding for either. The census and `corpus.classified` report both, which is what the control on OB-COV-1 declares, and no document says so.
facets.title: Spec 12 calls two Phase A outcomes structural findings and the engine emits none

facets.summary: Q31 rules that this repository becomes public and leaves the date unset. The date belongs to the owner alone, and no measurement, no build and no adopter produces one.
facets.title: The publication date of this repository is unset and the owner alone sets it

A session that meets the superseded register first either reaches the decision that replaced it or reports the stale answer.
Nothing makes a skill load, so its reach is a measurement, and this is the instrument that takes it.
